medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The College of Medicine’s mission prioritizes improving access to quality health care, reducing health disparities, promoting equity and improving the health of communities in Washington and beyond.

Resources:
•    Health Justice and Belonging: https://medicine.wsu.edu/hjb/
•	Student Diversity Center: https://spokane.wsu.edu/student-diversity/
•	SIGs: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/student-affairs/student-groups/
•	Scholarship support: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/student-affairs/financial-education-scholarships/
•	Equity Committee: https://medicine.wsu.edu/about/diversity-inclusion/health-equity/
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Students are encouraged to get involved in multiple ways. The College of Medicine provides opportunities for students to form Student Interest Groups (SIG) which are informal groups that meet with a faculty advisor about a particular topic. If a SIG wishes to organize a formal event or request funding they must become a Registered Student Organization (RSO) through WSU Spokane Office of Student Leadership and Involvement.

For more information, visit: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/student-affairs/student-groups/
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The Student Affairs’ mission is to help you succeed as a student, professional and individual from acceptance to practicing physician. We provide holistic support and guidance to help students achieve their highest potential to learn, lead, serve, and care for patients and their community. 
Support includes:
1. Financial education and literacy
2. Social connectedness to classmates and communities across Washington State
3. Student wellness programs and services
4. Wrap-around support for residency application and match processes
5. Clinical onboarding and compliance monitoring
6. Student support and advocacy
7. Promotion of inclusive environments with respectful dialogue
8. Celebrations of student successes and milestones

For more information visit: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/student-affairs/
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Washington State University Spokane does not provide on-campus housing for students. Courtesy of the Associated Students of WSU Spokane, all students with a WSU email address receive free access to Places4students, an online off-campus housing registry to assist students in finding housing, roommates, and sublets in Spokane.  Additionally, Student Affairs provides an online community via SLACK where students can connect with one another to find roommates and/or post housing needs within the College of Medicine student community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The WSU Health Sciences Spokane Student Diversity Center provides a list of resources to support students including gender and sexual minority students: https://spokane.wsu.edu/student-diversity/resources/. The College of Medicine has a LGBTIQ+ Health Student Interest Group. There is also a list of gender inclusive restrooms on campus: hhttps://spokane.wsu.edu/lactation-rooms-and-neutral-restrooms/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: We are a very mission-focused medical school. You will hear our mission spoken about frequently. We aim to promote an inclusive and supportive learning culture. We have a student collaboration hub (our large student lounge) which is for students only and includes small and group study rooms, study booths, a kitchen, and general gathering space.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students will be required to transport themselves to their Clinical Campus Weeks during the first two years (4 independent weeks when they will go to their clinical campus). Students will also need a vehicle to get themselves to and from clinical responsibilities in Years 3 and 4. Public transportation may not be available to/from all clinical training sites.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The Elson S. Floyd College of Medicine is fully accreditation by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME).

We have created an infrastructure for health care education and delivery that is bold, audacious, and visionary. Those three words, spoken by the late Washington State University President Elson S. Floyd, capture the essence of his idea for a second public medical school in the state. His goal was benevolent: to expand access to health care in medically underserved areas of Washington.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
To serve Washington and beyond through collaboration and problem-solving in education,
research, and health care with a focus on rural communities, Tribal Nations, and people who have been historically marginalized.

Our Mission in Action:
We seek to enroll candidates who most align with our mission and have similar goals to serve all WA communities, especially rural, Tribal nations, and those who have been historically marginalized. Below are some examples of how we enact our mission. 

Admissions:
•	Holistic Review: Our admissions process truly balances an applicant’s experiences and attributes with their metrics in alignment with our mission. Once a threshold combination of GPA and MCAT have been met for a secondary, we blind these metrics – no one ever sees MCAT and GPAs! . 
•	Focus on WA: We consider only those who have ties to/residency in WA. We ultimately hope our graduates will choose to practice in and care for WA communities. 
•	Experiences with rural and/or underserved communities: one of the key experiences we are looking for are those who come from or have experience with these communities.

Student Affairs: 
•	Financial education: Between 40-50% of our student body comes from low socioeconomically backgrounds. It is important that we have resources to support them. On our Student Affairs team, we have a Director for Financial Education who meets with students each year to build a plan for debt management. This provides our students with the insights to select a career specialty choice based on their passion rather than their debt.
•	Our student interest groups include those focused on the broad diversity including Student National Medical Student Association, Latino Medical Student Association, Women in Medicine, Military medicine, Non-Traditional Students, and LGBTQI+ Interest Group.
•	We partner with the WSU Spokane Office of Native American Health Sciences who helps support our American Indian and Alaska Native students. They also have a Center for Native American Health: https://nativehealth.wsu.edu/center-for-native-american-health/

Curriculum, Assessment, and Learning Support:
•	Rural/Urban Underserved Rotation: In Year 4, all students are required to complete a rural underserved or urban underserved 4-week rotation as a graduation requirement. 
•	Community-based medical school within a Land Grant institution: As a community-based medical school, we train our students across Washington and within diverse communities including rural, underserved, tribal clinics, and urban clinic/hospitals. This provides our students with broad exposure to diverse populations in WA to help inform them of the challenging health care problems that exist. https://medicine.wsu.edu/community/
•	Coaching: Every student will be assigned a faculty academic coach who will be with them all four years. This serves to further support our students toward self-learning and improvement. We also provide students with a USMLE Step 1 Coach. More info about our Student Learning Center: https://medicine.wsu.edu/about/departments-units/student-learning-center/

Graduates: 
•	Our alumni have begun practicing in Washington and serving the communities we hoped they'd serve. Learn more here: https://medicine.wsu.edu/alumni/md/

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes for accepted applicants prior to matriculation
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks for offers before April 30th. Time to respond will be reduced as matriculation approaches.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: A Health Professions Advisory Committee Packet will fulfill the minimum letter requirement. Letters must have been received from AMCAS in order to be considered for a secondary application; thus, the required letters deadline is before December 1st, the deadline for the secondary application, allowing time for our system to check for the letters and send out a secondary application and time to complete and return by the December 1st deadline.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
We do not require letters to be written by specific individuals; however, we encourage letters from faculty (if you are still in coursework or recently in school, or have conducted research or other academic pursuits), employment supervisors, volunteer supervisors, military command, etc. We do not want letters from friends, friends of family, and family members. Letters should come from academic, professional, and/or volunteer pursuits. 

Letters should also have current year listed for date (do not forward old letters for your new application if you are a reapplicant).
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: In addition to the interviews, the virtual interview day will include a student panel and detailed information about the admissions process.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Virtual Hybrid: 4 asynchronous interviews with a live moderator and 2 live virtual traditional structured interviews.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: We conduct a virtual interview season.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who 1) Have met a GPA/MCAT threshold combination; 2) meet a WA resident student definition or 3 of 4 ties to WA; US Citizen/Permanent Resident; all req'd letters rec'd from AMCAS
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Meet a "resident student" of WA definition or meets ties to WA as outlined on our website. International applicants are not accepted.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Must meet ties to Washington criteria or a definition of "resident student"
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Non-WA residents must meet 3 of 4 ties to WA to recieve a secondary or meet a military or tribal membership exception. Review our website: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/apply/requirements/
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
•	Letters of Evaluation: We require either 3 individual letters or a Health Professions Advisory Packet however, we do not weight one more than the other and do not stipulate whom letters come from only that they not be from family/friends, are written on letterhead, signed, and dated in the current year.  
•	We require the MCAT for a secondary because we only utilize the MCAT to meet one of our combination thresholds. We do not fill our interview spots until all completed applications (AMCAS, secondary, letters) have been considered for an interview. 

Applicants must meet four requirements to receive a secondary application; there are no exceptions made to these requirements. Please read our website thoroughly for these https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/apply/requirements/

To receive a secondary application, applicants must have connections to the state. Applicants who do not meet 3 of 4 ties to the state (as defined on our website) must meet one of the legal definitions of WA resident student (verified via requested documents):  
 
1) Applicants who are financially independent and have maintained a bona fide domicile in the state of Washington primarily for purposes other than educational for at least one year by and immediately leading into January 1 of the enrollment year.

2) Applicants who are financially dependent with at least one parent or legal guardian who has maintained a bona fide domicile in the state of Washington for at least one year by and immediately leading into January 1 of the enrollment year.

3) Applicants who are on active military duty stationed in the state of Washington or are members of the Washington national guard.

4) Applicants who (i) are members of a federally recognized tribe whose traditional and customary tribal boundaries include portions of the state of Washington, or whose tribe was granted reserved lands within the state of Washington, and (ii) have maintained a bona fide domicile in Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington or a combination of these states, for one year by and immediately leading into January 1 of the enrollment year.

Applicants who claim WA residency and do not meet the ties to the state will be required to submit documentation proving one of the definitions above. 

We also established three threshold combinations of GPA and MCAT; we utilize the AMCAS calculated GPA. There are no exceptions to these thresholds (graduate GPA may be considered if these thresholds are not met with the UGPA). Review our website for more info: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/apply/requirements/ 
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.8 – 4.0, then 27th percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.4 – 3.79, then 43rd percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 2.6 – 3.39, then 61st percentile rank or higher on the MCAT

Once all secondary requirements have been met, an applicant will be sent the secondary application. Upon return of the secondary, we mask MCAT and GPA from further review through the remainder of our process. From that point forward, we only consider experiences and attributes as they relate to our mission in deciding who we interview and accept. Per state and federal law, we also mask race/ethnicity in our process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
We consider the MCAT in combination with the undergraduate GPA to receive a secondary application. Applicants must meet one of the following:

- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.8 – 4.0, then 27th percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.4 – 3.79, then 43rd percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 2.6 – 3.39, then 61st percentile rank or higher on the MCAT

If the UGPA is not sufficient to meet one of these threshold combinations, we will consider a GGPA if taken in science or medical science coursework. More info on these threshold combinations can be found here: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/apply/requirements/

Once one of these combination thresholds are met to receive a secondary, we COMPLETELY mask the MCAT and GPAs from further review by all (screeners, interviewers, and Admissions Committee members) through the entirety of our process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: 27th percentile rank. This translated MCAT score requires a UGPA of 3.8 or higher (see threshold combinations above)
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: 2.6 Undergraduate GPA. This GPA requires a score in the 61st percentile rank on the MCAT (see threshold combinations above)
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo:
We consider the MCAT in combination with the undergraduate GPA to receive a secondary application. Applicants must meet one of the following:

- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.8 – 4.0, then 27th percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.4 – 3.79, then 43rd percentile rank or higher on the MCAT
- If undergraduate cumulative GPA is 2.6 – 3.39, then 61st percentile rank or higher on the MCAT

If the UGPA is not sufficient to meet one of these threshold combinations, we will consider a GGPA if taken in science or medical science coursework. More info on these threshold combinations can be found here: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/apply/requirements/
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We need enough graduate work to be able to be able to forgo the UGPA and assess this requirement based on GGPA. The minimum to the left does not guarantee a secondary.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Provided that the community college is regionally accredited, we accept any community college coursework, including for pre-requisites, regardless of the the purpose for attending. We understand applicants have varying pathways, opportunities, access, and reasons for attending community college, and we fully support that in our process.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We do not accept/consider letter of intent/interest or updates from applicants at any point in our process. We only consider the official documents submitted via the application process to make interview and selection decisions. We believe this helps maintain an equitable process for all applicants.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The WSU College of Medicine offers a unique resource in the Financial Educator who helps medical students with their financial goals and offers guidance on scholarships. 

Programming includes:
•	Monthly MedMoney sessions on financial education topics
•	1:1 sessions tailored to students' individual needs (debt management, budgeting, credit reports/score, loans and payment options, scholarships
•	Weekly financial posts w/ reminders, videos, scholarship deadlines and short documents on relevant topics

Student Financial Services: https://medicine.wsu.edu/md/student-affairs/financial-education-scholarships/

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants will be notified if they are on the waitlist after their Admissions Committee meeting. The official rank list is formed in mid-March at which time applicants can request their rank.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: We only have three required courses and do not waive these. Despite only having three course requirements, we highly encourage applicants to take the necessary courses to prepare for medical school.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites:
Facebook:  WSU Elson S. Floyd College of Medicine
Twitter: @WSUMedicine
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: We utilize a mission-aligned process whereby after meeting one of the MCAT/GPA threshold combinations, experiences and attributes are considered heavily toward meeting our mission; MCAT and GPA are no longer considered after the secondary is returned. We are seeking applicants with experiences in rural communities, with Tribal Nations, or with those who have been historically marginalized, those who are committed to serving Washington and have strong ties to our state, those with clinical exposure and time spent in non-health care community-serving activities, and experience beyond the classroom. We also are looking for applicants with the following attributes: leadership, communication, intellectual excellence, ethical responsibility to yourself and others, resilience/adaptability, and teamwork/collaboration.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Clinical exposure: Quality of experience (including shadowing, scribe, helping care within your family, emergency medical technician) AND amount of exposure.
